Agreed: today the Dafny file proves the model, the tests sample the code, and nothing ties the two together. Which validation do you want built for BE-033?

options.label: Model as oracle + mutation (Recommended)
options.description: Compile KernelProtocol.dfy to Python, as MemoryBackend.dfy already is. The kernel's real exits are then checked against the proved model, exhaustively over the whole finite space (routes, exits, runtimes, closable, posture) instead of by sampling. Then run the repo's mutation tooling (pytest-gremlins via run_mutate) on the protocol code to measure which code changes the tests actually catch. This ties model and code together and measures test strength. It adds one compiled oracle and a CI step; about M effort.

options.label: Exhaustive enumeration only
options.description: Replace the Hypothesis sampling with a generated suite over the full finite exit space, as test_condition_space.py does for other clauses. Every combination runs every time, and no Dafny build is involved. Stronger than sampling, but the model and the code are still not linked. About S effort.

options.label: TLA+ for close/run races
options.description: Model concurrent close against in-flight calls in sdd/formal/tla/ and run the TLC model checker on it. This is the only option that covers concurrency, which neither the tests nor Dafny touch. But the race belongs to the Session, which doesn't exist yet, so this is BK-455's scope. About M effort, and it delays this PR.

options.label: Keep PR, file item
options.description: Leave this PR as it is and file a backlog item for linking model and code. It records the gap, and the PR stays smaller.

How far should mutation testing go in this PR?

options.label: kernel.py + weekly scope (Recommended)
options.description: Mutation-test the async kernel.py now and kill any protocol survivors with new cells. Also add a kernel scope to scripts/mutate_scopes.py so the weekly mutation CI keeps covering src/remote_store/_kernel/. A local run takes about 15 minutes or more.

options.label: kernel.py only
options.description: Mutate kernel.py now and fix the survivors. Don't change the weekly CI scope, so the PR stays smaller.

options.label: Weekly scope only
options.description: Add only the CI scope, and leave the kernel.py findings to the first weekly run as a follow-up.

options.label: Stop here
options.description: Record the current results (_io.py 20/20, 45/62 overall) in the trace, and go on to /ship round 3.

questions.question: What about the 14 survivors in backend.py that aren't protocol code?

options.label: Backlog item (Recommended)
options.description: File a new BK item for the _RangeReader, _HandleStream and _SPOOL_MAX survivors. That keeps this PR scoped to the protocol.

options.label: Fix in this PR
options.description: Add cells that kill them now. This widens the PR beyond BK-449.

options.label: Ignore
options.description: Note them in the trace only.

questions.question: How far should mutation testing on the kernel go?

options.label: Add kernel scope to weekly CI (Recommended)
options.description: Add a scope for src/remote_store/_kernel/ tested by tests/_kernel/ to scripts/mutate_scopes.py, so the weekly mutation run covers kernel.py too, without slowing this PR. Any kernel.py survivors show up in the weekly report.

options.label: Also mutate kernel.py now
options.description: Run gremlins on kernel.py in this PR (about 15+ min per run) and add tests for the protocol survivors before round 3. The PR takes longer but is more thorough.

options.label: Stop here
options.description: Keep what has run so far. kernel.py stays untested by mutation, and only the model-based sweep covers it.

questions.question: After that, how should the review loop continue?

options.label: Run /ship to convergence (Recommended)
options.description: Round 3 onward, then the unprimed, whole-file and measuring checks, then paste the ship-report review block into the trace. I report back when the PR is ready to merge.

options.label: One more round, then report
options.description: Run only round 3 and stop for your review again.

options.label: Pause
options.description: Do nothing more. I stay subscribed to the PR and only respond to CI and review events.

questions.question: Should the weekly mutation CI cover the kernel's protocol code from now on?

options.label: Add derived kernel scope (Recommended)
options.description: Add src/remote_store/_kernel/ with tests/_kernel/ to scripts/mutate_scopes.py, derived like the existing scopes. A future protocol regression in _io.py or aio_backend.py then shows up as a survivor every week. This PR grows by one small script change plus its test.

options.label: Leave it out of this PR
options.description: Track it as a new backlog item instead. The PR stays smaller, but nothing re-runs mutation testing on the protocol code until that item is done.

questions.question: What should happen with the code that has not been mutation-tested or still has survivors?

options.label: Mutate kernel.py now (Recommended)
options.description: kernel.py holds the guard, the write try/finally and _cleanup_failed, so it is protocol code that has not been mutated yet. A run takes about 10 to 15 minutes, and I would add cells for any protocol survivors. The 14 backend.py survivors are not protocol code, so they go to a backlog item.

options.label: kernel.py and backend.py
options.description: Also kill the 14 backend.py survivors (_RangeReader, _HandleStream, _SPOOL_MAX). That widens the PR beyond BK-449's scope.

options.label: Neither, backlog both
options.description: Record both gaps as backlog items and move on to the review.

questions.question: Once that is done, how should the review continue?

options.label: /ship round 3 to close (Recommended)
options.description: Run the scoped round 3, then the closing gates (unprimed, whole-file, measuring), and paste the ship-report review block into the trace.

options.label: Stop after the mutation work
options.description: Push the mutation work, report back, and wait for you again before any review round.

Should the generated diagram land in the repo?

options.label: Generated into spec, in this PR (Recommended)
options.description: Add scripts/gen_protocol_diagram.py with a --check mode in preflight, like gen_graph. It writes a fenced, generated block under BE-033 in spec 003. If KernelProtocol.dfy changes and the oracle is rebuilt, a stale diagram fails the gate. Adds one script, one test file and a block in the spec to this PR.

options.label: Backlog item, after this PR
options.description: Record it as a new BK item with this prototype in the dossier. This PR stays as it is.

options.label: One-off only
options.description: Keep it in the scratchpad as a one-off look. Nothing lands, and nothing keeps it current.

questions.question: If it lands, where should the diagram be visible?

options.label: Spec 003 BE-033 (Recommended)
options.description: Next to the States and Transitions tables it illustrates. GitHub renders Mermaid there.

options.label: Spec plus custom-backend guide
options.description: Also show it to backend authors in docs-src/guides/custom-backend-guide.md. That needs a mkdocs Mermaid check and is a second generated block to keep current.

options.label: sdd/formal/README.md
options.description: Next to the oracle description, aimed at readers of the formal models rather than spec readers.
